claims.text: Spin-polarized density functional theory calculations can be used to predict the presence of ferromagnetic ground states.
Satisfaction of the Stoner criterion indicates that a spin-polarized ferromagnetic state can be stabilized.
The initial material has a non-magnetically ordered electronic structure.
The initial material has a high density of states near the Fermi level.
Spin-polarized DFT, optionally including Hubbard U corrections, can compute the relevant electronic structure.
Exchange splitting in the electronic band structure is a mediator of ferromagnetic stabilization.
A high density of states at the Fermi level together with sufficiently strong electron-electron interactions lowers the energy of the spin-polarized state.
Energy lowering of the spin-polarized state stabilizes ferromagnetism.
The spin-polarized ferromagnetic calculation will have a lower total energy than the non-magnetic calculation.
The lower-energy spin-polarized solution will exhibit a measurable magnetic moment.
A non-magnetic DFT calculation shows no exchange splitting.
The non-magnetic DFT state has a higher total energy than the ferromagnetic state.
Predictive reliability depends on whether the exchange-correlation functional and any Hubbard U correction adequately describe electron-electron interactions.
The proposed method may not be predictive for strongly correlated materials or systems with significant disorder.
